title: Baeckea frutescens Suppresses Melanogenesis via Modulation of PKA/CREB and ERK/MAPK Pathways: Insights from Cellular, Zebrafish, and In Silico Analyses.
authors: Yu, Chih-Li; Huang, Yen-Li; Huang, Yingying; Zhong, Yu; Pang, Haiyue; Wang, Guey-Horng
one_liner_zh: 该文研究植物提取物抑制黑色素生成的信号通路机制，与蛋白质-DNA互作及TF-DNA结合建模完全无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Baeckea frutescens L. (BF) has been reported as a potential natural source for skin-whitening agents. However, its antimelanogenic activity and mechanisms remain unclear. METHODS: The antimelanogenic effects of BF were evaluated in alpha-melanocyte-stimulating hormone (alpha-MSH)-stimulated B16F10 cells and in zebrafish embryos. Cell viability, intracellular tyrosinase activity and melanin content were measured. Western blot (WB) analysis was used to examine melanogenesis-related proteins. Network pharmacology and molecular docking were performed to predict potential targets and interactions of BF-derived metabolites. RESULTS: The ethanolic extract of BF reduced intracellular tyrosinase activity and melanin content in cells without cytotoxicity. Western blot analysis showed decreased expression of microphthalmia-associated transcription factor (MITF) and its downstream melanogenic enzymes, including tyrosinase (TYR), tyrosinase-related protein-1 (TRP-1), and dopachrome tautomerase (DCT). In addition, BF reduced phosphorylation of protein kinase A (PKA), cAMP responsive element-binding protein (CREB) and extracellular signal-regulated kinase (ERK), suggesting potential suppression of PKA/CREB and ERK signaling pathways. These regulatory effects may contribute to MITF downregulation and subsequent inhibition of melanogenesis. BF reduced melanin accumulation in zebrafish embryos. Network pharmacology and molecular docking analyses further suggested that BF-derived metabolites, particularly bayogenin, may interact with multiple melanogenesis-related targets. CONCLUSIONS: BF may inhibit melanogenesis through coordinated modulation of multiple signaling pathways and may represent a promising skin-whitening candidate.
abstract_zh: 背景：据报道，岗松（Baeckea frutescens L.，BF）是皮肤美白剂的潜在天然来源。然而，其抗黑色素生成活性及机制仍不清楚。方法：在α-黑素细胞刺激激素（alpha-MSH）刺激的B16F10细胞和斑马鱼胚胎中评估BF的抗黑色素生成效果。测量了细胞活力、细胞内酪氨酸酶活性和黑色素含量。使用蛋白质印迹（Western blot，WB）分析检查黑色素生成相关蛋白。进行网络药理学和分子对接以预测BF衍生代谢物的潜在靶点和相互作用。结果：BF的乙醇提取物在无细胞毒性情况下降低了细胞内酪氨酸酶活性和黑色素含量。Western blot分析显示，小眼畸形相关转录因子（MITF）及其下游黑色素生成酶（包括酪氨酸酶（TYR）、酪氨酸酶相关蛋白-1（TRP-1）和多巴色素互变异构酶（DCT））的表达降低。此外，BF降低了蛋白激酶A（PKA）、cAMP反应元件结合蛋白（CREB）和细胞外信号调节激酶（ERK）的磷酸化，提示可能抑制PKA/CREB和ERK信号通路。这些调节效应可能有助于MITF下调及随后的黑色素生成抑制。BF减少了斑马鱼胚胎中的黑色素积累。网络药理学和分子对接分析进一步表明，BF衍生代谢物，特别是bayogenin，可能与多个黑色素生成相关靶点相互作用。结论：BF可能通过协调调节多条信号通路抑制黑色素生成，并可能成为有前景的美白候选物。
